question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945712/assets/5548481ccbe3aee88fd4b346ad53777b7101223c19f7e8408c8ef85bb0d9df25.png)

Given the right triangle $△PQR$ shown above, which of the following diagrams represents the height corresponding to $\overset{―}{PR}?$
question.worked_solution:
The height (or altitude) corresponding to $\overset{―}{PR}$ is a line segment that 

- runs from the opposite vertex $Q$ to the line $\overset{⟷}{PR},$ and

- is perpendicular to $\overset{⟷}{PR}.$

The correct diagram is shown below.

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HAC+m∠BAC & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HAC+{110}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HAC & ={70}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HCA+m∠HAC+m∠AHC & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA+{70}^{∘}+{90}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA+{160}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA & ={20}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
